elements.element: Early-termination fee is capped at 3 months' fees
elements.evidence: "equal to the lesser of (i) the aggregate Net Sales ... divided by two, and (ii) the aggregate fees payable by the Company to HDI under Section 3.1 in respect of the three (3) calendar months preceding the Termination Date"—the lesser-of construction ensures the payment never exceeds 3 months' fees

elements.element: The capped fee is the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer on termination
elements.evidence: "the Termination Payment shall be the only amount payable by the Company by reason of termination"

elements.element: No liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer at all
elements.evidence: "the Company shall pay to HDI a termination payment" is retained, merely capped

offending_extra_words: No Termination Payment shall be due if the Company terminates this Agreement pursuant to Section 1.6 or as a result of HDI's breach of this Agreement,
reasons: Fallback is fully satisfied: the lesser-of operator caps the Termination Payment at three months' fees payable under Section 3.1, and the payment is expressly stated to be the only amount payable by reason of termination.
Preferred (no liquidated amount at all) is not met, which is acceptable since the locked target is the fallback.

Minimality fails: the edit adds a broad new exception excusing any Termination Payment where the Company terminates under Section 1.6 or for HDI's breach. That is a separate commercial win not required to complete the fallback cap.

Deterministic gates confirm over-editing: operation 1 expands 34 words to 107 (ratio 3.15) and changes 69% of characters; the cap could have been achieved by inserting the lesser-of limb plus a short sole-remedy phrase.
Cross-reference to "Section 1.6" is unverified in the supplied text and risks a dangling mechanic; if retained it should be confirmed against the executed agreement.
Untouched terms (payment in eight quarterly instalments, Net Sales formula as the alternative limb) remain effective, so commercial intent is otherwise preserved.
